outcomes.text: Understand factual details and abstract ideas in texts about general subjects.
Locate and choose relevant information from longer texts in different formats.
Recognise emotions, attitudes, and opinions that are directly stated or implied.
Follow arguments and conclusions in discursive writing and distinguish facts from opinions.
Understand texts written in a range of language registers.
Work out unfamiliar vocabulary from context across varied subjects.
Understand broad vocabulary and varied grammatical structures, including some complex sentences.
Communicate facts, ideas, opinions, and arguments about general subjects.
Write arguments explaining advantages and disadvantages while supporting a viewpoint.
Expand arguments with relevant supporting details and examples.
Produce detailed, assured descriptions and narratives of real or imaginary experiences.
Organise ideas into coherent paragraphs and longer texts using cohesive devices.
Use register, style, and genre conventions appropriate to the purpose.
Use extensive vocabulary, including relevant idioms, with reasonable accuracy.
Use varied grammatical structures, including complex forms, with reasonable accuracy.
Communicate facts, ideas, opinions, and arguments about complex subjects.
Develop arguments by evaluating important issues and supporting viewpoints with reasons and examples.
Read varied literary works independently, recognising implicit meanings and ideas.
Explain how language choices and textual features create effects for readers.
Critically assess themes, characters, ideas, and details while recognising genre conventions.
Give a supported personal interpretation of literary themes and characters.
Organise ideas into coherent paragraphs and extended written responses.
Discuss friends, family, relationships, generation gaps and changing family structures.
Examine quality of life, living environments, urban and rural differences, overcrowding and social isolation.
Discuss lifestyle choices involving relationships, diet, fashion, self-expression, values and personal goals.
Understand inclusivity, diversity, gender equality and social mobility.
Explore ageism, racism and classism as forms of social prejudice.
Understand immigration, refugee experiences and integration.
Understand social organisation, law and order, governance and communities.
Explore national and global citizenship.
Examine the rights and responsibilities of individuals and governments.
Understand global warming, climate change, pollution, solutions, government action and economic effects.
Explore biodiversity conservation, ecosystems and the treatment of animals.
Consider the effects of population growth.
Understand natural-resource use, recycling, waste management and consumer overconsumption.
Compare energy sources, including fossil fuels and renewables, and examine related geopolitics and environmental effects.
Explore ways to reduce environmental impact through choices about housing, food and travel.
Understand sustainable tourism and the benefits of travel.
Consider global cooperation and its tensions with national priorities.
Examine individual, industrial and governmental roles in environmental protection, including environmental movements.
Understand popular entertainment forms such as cinema, television, streaming, gaming and the internet.
Discuss the role of entertainment in people’s lives.
Explore celebrity culture, including role models, idols and public responsibilities.
Examine how style, appearance, language, group affiliation and fashion express identity.
Understand the preservation and respectful treatment of cultural heritage, monuments, festivals and traditions.
Explore theatre, music, visual arts, dance, literature and film.
Discuss access to the arts, funding, awards, representation and diversity.
Explore medical advances and ethical issues in scientific research.
Understand smart technology, privacy and security.
Understand artificial intelligence.
Examine digital media, including its benefits and dangers.
Explore communication technology and online communities.
Consider access to technology.
Explore the use of technology in education.
Explore the use of technology in the workplace.
